title: THREE WORLDS, ONE FACT
goal: Keep several explanations alive until new evidence separates them.
steps:
1. Keep Event — Keep the event fixed.
2. Invent — Invent three models for why it happened.
3. Predict Different — Each model must predict a different thing you could observe next.
4. Earliest — Notice the earliest observation that would separate them.
5. Speak Plurals — Until that evidence arrives, speak in plurals: possibilities, not prophecy.
win: One event produced multiple testable possibilities instead of a single prediction dressed as certainty.
supports:
• Check what you actually know; look for one missing fact.
• Ask what else could fit; separate possibility from probability.
• Delay major conclusions when upset; separate guess from evidence.
• Ask what would disprove it; use recent, concrete evidence.
• Delay the verdict; use current facts.
formula_flow: Keep Event → Invent → Predict Different → Earliest → Speak Plurals
safety:
PAUSE
Do not multiply theories when an urgent practical response is already clear.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ADD THE PREFIX
goal: Notice the thought as mental activity, then keep doing what you chose.
steps:
1. Prefix Thought — Put “I am noticing my mind produce…” before the thought. Say the whole sentence once at normal speed.
2. Check Command — Notice what remains true and what loses command authority.
3. Resume Task — Carry on with the next chosen task while the sentence exists nearby.
win: The thought remained present without deciding what your hands or attention did next.
supports:
• Start physically; shrink the first action.
• Reward starting, not finishing; choose tiny action.
• Cut the task; make it visible.
• Skip extra setup; lower the first demand.
• Begin while unsure; choose a rough beginning.
formula_flow: Prefix Thought → Check Command → Resume Task
safety:
PAUSE
Drop the wording if it feels mocking, unreal, or destabilising.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THANKS, MIND. NO CONTRACT.
goal: Respect the warning in a thought without letting it sign the contract.
steps:
1. Ask Danger — Ask what danger the thought is trying to prevent.
2. Thank Intention — Offer a precise thank-you for that intention.
3. Answer M — Answer: “I’m not signing this instruction.” Choose one action that reflects what matters to you while keeping any useful caution.
4. Respect — Respect the alarm; decline the contract.
win: You kept the useful caution and still chose one action that matched what matters.
supports:
• Do not wait for motivation; name what matters today.
• Use one priority; keep meaning practical.
• Choose one value-led action; accept the trade-off.
• Protect important time; use values to choose trade-offs.
• Remove one conflict; pick one value for this decision.
formula_flow: Ask Danger → Thank Intention → Answer M → Respect
safety:
PAUSE
Do not dismiss warnings that point to concrete and immediate danger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THOUGHT DEPARTURES
goal: Watch a thought arrive and leave without helping it stay or go.
steps:
1. Place Thought — Place the thought on something imagined as moving: a bus, leaf, or subtitle.
2. Watch Arrival — Watch its full arrival and departure without pushing it faster.
3. Return Eyes — When the carrier exits, return your eyes to one fixed visual point.
4. Allow Departure — Another carrier may come; none owns the station.
win: The thought completed one imagined journey while your attention returned to something real.
supports:
• Test the assumption; use a real example.
• Ask what would disprove it; notice absolute words like always.
• Look for one missing fact; use current facts.
• Use recent, concrete evidence; ask what else could fit.
• Separate guess from evidence; avoid treating guesses as facts.
formula_flow: Place Thought → Watch Arrival → Return Eyes → Allow Departure
safety:
PAUSE
Stop imagery if it increases detachment from surroundings.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: NAME THE SERIES
goal: Recognise the recurring story before treating today's episode as new evidence.
steps:
1. Ignore — Ignore today’s plot for ten seconds.
2. Ask Recurring — Ask what recurring series it belongs to: ‘The Rejection prediction,’ ‘Everyone Is Ahead,’ ‘I Must Fix It Now.’ Give the series a short title and season number.
3. Ask Whether — Then check if this episode contains new information or recycled footage.
win: You named the series and could tell what was fresh versus recycled.
supports:
• Notice what you cannot see; limit social media exposure.
• Notice hidden differences; return to your priorities.
• Name one thing already working; use your own priorities.
• Use your own timeline; keep context visible.
• Track progress by your values; return to your own baseline.
formula_flow: Ignore → Ask Recurring → Ask Whether
safety:
PAUSE
Retire any title that ridicules genuine pain or identity.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PASSENGER THOUGHT
goal: Complete one meaningful action while the unwanted thought rides along.
steps:
1. Choose Time — Choose one two-minute action that matters.
2. Ride Passenger — Invite the thought to ride in the passenger seat—audible, uncomfortable, unedited.
3. Keep Hands — Hold hands on the action wheel and complete the movement while it talks.
4. Who Drove? — At the destination, notice who actually drove.
win: The two-minute action finished even though the thought never had to disappear.
supports:
• Do the easiest useful part; remove one barrier.
• Make it visible; remove one obvious distraction.
• Start with one minute; open only what you need.
• Prepare the task in advance; shrink the first action.
• Lower standards briefly; use two minutes.
formula_flow: Choose Time → Ride Passenger → Keep Hands → Who Drove?
safety:
PAUSE
Shorten the trip if functioning or situational awareness drops.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MAKE A WIDER CONTAINER
goal: Make more room around a difficult sensation instead of trying to remove it.
steps:
1. Locate Unwanted — Locate the unwanted sensation.
2. Find Edges — Find its edges.
3. Soften Muscles — Soften the muscles around—not inside—it.
4. Include Neutral — Include one neutral body area and one external sound in awareness.
5. Widen the Room — You are enlarging the room, not evicting the guest.
win: The sensation shared awareness with a neutral body area and an outside sound.
supports:
• Review the cost; remove one conflicting commitment.
• Keep the action small; protect important time.
• Choose aligned action; accept the trade-off.
• Name what matters today; review what the action costs.
• Name today's value; remove one conflict.

title: PAIN PLUS THE FIGHT
goal: Separate the pain itself from the extra fight you are adding.
steps:
1. Make Two Lanes — Imagine two lanes: WHAT HURTS and WHAT RESISTANCE ADDS.
2. Keep The Hurt — In the first lane, picture the raw sensation or fact.
3. Catch The Fight — In the second lane, name demands, self-attack, bracing, and impossible arguments with reality.
4. Drop One Fight — Release one item from the resistance lane while respecting the hurt.
win: One layer of self-attack, bracing, or impossible demand was dropped while the hurt remained respected.
supports:
• Prefer repair; separate guilt from responsibility.
• Name the exact mistake; drop self-punishment.
• Use the same standard for everyone; name the mistake.
• Recall capability; name what was outside your control.
• Use equal standards; choose one repair.
formula_flow: Make Two Lanes → Keep The Hurt → Catch The Fight → Drop One Fight
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use acceptance language to tolerate abuse, injustice, or untreated symptoms.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ENTER THE ACTION
goal: Re-enter an ordinary activity through your senses instead of demanding perfect focus.
steps:
1. Choose Ordinary — Choose one ordinary activity.
2. Place Vision — Place vision, touch, posture, and hearing inside it.
3. Leave Re — When attention leaves, re-enter through the next physical contact point rather than scolding yourself.
4. Stay Activity — Stay until the activity reaches its natural edge.
5. Enter Fully — Participation, not perfect focus, is the target.
win: Attention wandered and returned through the next physical contact point without self-scolding.
supports:
• Define good enough first; separate important errors from polish.
• Set a hard finish time; limit checking passes.
• Ship useful work; limit checking.
• Compare against the brief; make rough version.
• Make the rough version first; set finish time.

title: THE ATTENTION BOUNCER
goal: Decide which thought deserves attention instead of letting every thought enter.
steps:
1. Spot Arrival — Notice the next thought without following it.
2. Stamp Access — Stamp it REQUESTED, RELEVANT, or UNINVITED.
3. Set Budget — Give the chosen category five slow counts; let the others wait without argument.
4. Return Door — After five counts, return to the task or deliberately admit one new thought.
win: One thought received deliberate attention while the rest waited without a fight.
supports:
• Silence nonessential notifications; use one window at a time.
• Finish or park one open loop; return to one target.
• Mute alerts; choose one target.
• Close what you do not need; protect one focus block.
• Reduce nearby noise; keep one task visible.

safety:
PAUSE

title: EMOTION, COMPLETE YOUR ARC
goal: Let an emotion complete one natural bodily shift before choosing what the situation needs.
steps:
1. Locate Emotion — Locate the emotion in the body and give it a precise name.
2. Permit — Permit its current intensity without feeding the story.
3. Track Sensation — Track where sensation travels, peaks, breaks, or cools.
4. Follow Appears — Follow until one natural shift appears, then choose the action the situation—not the wave—requires.
win: The sensation changed somewhere—movement, peak, break, or cooling—before you acted.
supports:
• Use simple words for the problem; name the emotion.
• Check the facts separately; name the feeling plainly.
• Lower nearby noise; eat, drink, or rest if needed.
• Delay the message; rest before deciding.
• Notice body tension; lower stimulation for a minute.
formula_flow: Locate Emotion → Permit → Track Sensation → Follow Appears
safety:
PAUSE
Seek help for escalating self-harm, aggression, panic, or inability to function.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE 2% SOFTENING
goal: Test whether a tiny believable softening changes the body's defensive setting.
steps:
1. Release Forehead — Without forcing happiness, release the forehead, loosen the eyes, and lift the mouth corners by two percent.
2. Keep Expression — Keep the expression believable.
3. Hold Neutral — Hold it while resting your gaze on one neutral visual point.
4. Ask Whether — Ask whether defence changed by even half a notch.
win: One facial area eased slightly and you noticed whether defence shifted at all.
supports:
• Sip water if it helps; keep your body supported.
• Give the surge time to pass; reduce caffeine.
• Reduce extra stimulation; avoid symptom searching.
• Unclench your jaw and shoulders; use ordinary surroundings.
• Keep movements gentle; loosen your shoulders.

safety:

title: PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD
goal: Use a slow movement sequence to prove your body can follow deliberate instructions.
steps:
1. Set Code — Choose three tiny comfortable movements, such as tap a knee, touch a thumb, and shift your gaze.
2. Run Order — Do A–B–C slowly, pausing after each movement long enough to feel it finish.
3. Reverse Code — Do C–B–A at the same pace. If you lose the order, restart instead of speeding up.
4. Claim Control — Name the movement you directed most clearly, then let the code stop.
win: You completed the pattern forward and backward without speeding through a mistake.
supports:
• Sip water if it helps; wait out the surge.
• Keep your body supported; unclench your jaw.
• Reduce extra stimulation; let breathing stay natural.
• Give the surge time to pass; let breaths happen.
• Loosen your shoulders; look at ordinary objects nearby.
formula_flow: Set Code → Run Order → Reverse Code → Claim Control
safety:
PAUSE
Do not play while driving, moving through hazards, dizzy, injured, or unable to stay oriented.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE FOUR-LETTER BRAKE
goal: Interrupt momentum long enough to choose the smallest safe move.
steps:
1. Stop Nonessential — Stop every nonessential movement.
2. Take Physical — Take one physical step back.
3. Observe Facts — Observe facts, sensations, and the strongest impulse.
4. Proceed Safely — Proceed with the smallest safe move that will still make sense in an hour.
5. Skip Negotiation — Do not negotiate with momentum between letters.
win: Facts, sensations, and impulse were noticed before your next action happened.
supports:
• Avoid bargaining; change locations.
• Tell someone if the urge spikes; leave the trigger.
• Change rooms if possible; delay ten minutes.
• Do one incompatible activity; make access harder.
• Ride the peak; avoid bargaining with the urge.

• Avoid bargaining; change locations.
• Tell someone if the urge spikes; leave the trigger.

• Do one incompatible activity; make access harder.
• Ride the peak; avoid bargaining with the urge.

title: EXHALE IN CHAPTERS
goal: Let the exhale leave in soft sections, then wait for the next inhale.
steps:
1. Let Air — Instead of one continuous out-breath, let air leave in three soft portions with tiny unforced spaces between.
2. Keep Face — Keep the face loose and never push to empty.
3. Wait Body — After the final segment, wait for the body’s next inhale rather than grabbing it.
win: Three gentle portions finished without pushing empty, and the body supplied the next breath on its own.
supports:
• Look at ordinary objects nearby; stop body scanning.
• Let breaths happen; keep your body supported.
• Reduce caffeine; avoid symptom searching.
• Loosen your shoulders; sip water if it helps.
• Use ordinary surroundings; wait out the surge.
formula_flow: Let Air → Keep Face → Wait Body
safety:
PAUSE
Resume normal breathing if segmentation causes urgency or tingling.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LET THE FIELD SELF-PUBLISH
goal: Let sights, sounds, sensations, and thoughts take turns without choosing a favourite.
steps:
1. Open Field — Open Field with sight, sound, sensation, and thought available at once.
2. Whatever — Notice whatever becomes prominent, then what replaces it.
3. Let All Arrive — Do not select, rank, or hold any item.
4. Track the Shift — Track the changing editorial order for one minute.
win: The foreground changed several times while you neither ranked nor held what appeared.
supports:
• Question absolute words; check the whole situation.
• Notice absolute words like always; separate guess from evidence.
• Ask what would disprove it; avoid treating guesses as facts.
• Add the missing context; delay major conclusions when upset.
• Check the base rate; ask what else could fit.
formula_flow: Open Field → Whatever → Let All Arrive → Track the Shift
safety:
PAUSE
Open monitoring should stop if unstructured awareness feels overwhelming.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: NO FAVOURITE SENSATION
goal: Give pleasant, unpleasant, dull, and vivid sensations the same brief welcome.
steps:
1. Let Field — Let the field choose its next foreground.
2. Pleasant — Pleasant, unpleasant, dull, or vivid—offer each the same brief hospitality.
3. Include Movement — When preference reaches to grip or reject, include that movement too.
4. End Whole — End by noticing the whole room at once.
win: Preference itself became another event in the field instead of deciding what had to stay or leave.
supports:
• Notice the first automatic moment; remove easy access.
• Replace one response; interrupt the sequence.
• Move the cue; reset after slips.
• Use the same replacement repeatedly; make the old habit harder.
• Notice the trigger; delay the routine.

safety:
PAUSE
Use a stable anchor instead during high body alarm or feeling unreal or disconnected.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: EXPAND–GATHER–EXPAND
goal: Move from the whole moment to the breath, then back out to wider awareness.
steps:
1. Acknowledge — First, acknowledge the full weather of the moment.
2. Breathe Small — Next, gather attention around breathing as a small centre.
3. Widen Whole — Finally, widen to the whole body and surrounding space.
4. Spend — Spend roughly one minute in each shape.
5. Carry Final — Carry the final wide frame into your next movement.
win: Attention narrowed around breathing and reopened to body plus surrounding space before you moved on.
supports:
• Wait before sending messages; let intensity fall.
• Use simple words for the problem; separate feeling from fact.
• Lower nearby noise; give the feeling time to move.
• Eat, drink, or rest if needed; use plain language.
• Notice what changed physically; name the emotion.
formula_flow: Acknowledge → Breathe Small → Widen Whole → Spend → Carry Final
safety:
PAUSE
Use a non-breath anchor if respiration is activating.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RAIN WITHOUT THE UMBRELLA
goal: Acknowledge what is here, meet it kindly, and remember it is not all of you.
steps:
1. Recognise — Recognise what is here.
2. Allow Moment — Allow this moment of it to exist.

5. Move R — Move through R–A–I–N once; resolution is not a required fifth letter.
win: The experience was recognised, allowed, gently investigated, and placed inside a larger sense of self.

• Rest before deciding; use plain language.

title: FOUR PARTS OF ONE STEP
goal: Walk slowly enough to notice the four physical parts of each step.
steps:
1. Place Weight — Slow enough to separate lift, travel, place, and weight transfer.
2. Follow Events — Follow those four events through several steps.
3. Thought — When thought pulls away, rejoin at whichever phase the foot is currently performing.
4. Finish Walking — Finish by walking normally while retaining one point of contact.
win: Attention rejoined the foot at its current phase whenever thought pulled away.
supports:
• Take a short break; return to one target.
• Return after interruptions; park secondary tasks.
• Put the phone out of reach; reduce background noise.
• Close extra tabs; protect one focus block.
• Use one screen; clear visual clutter.
formula_flow: Place Weight → Follow Events → Thought → Finish Walking
safety:
PAUSE
Practise only where slowed walking is physically safe.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LISTEN PAST THE SOUND
goal: Follow a sound all the way into silence without replaying it in memory.
steps:
1. Play Safe — Ring, play, or notice a safe sustained sound.
2. Follow Decay — Follow its decay with precision until you cannot locate any remainder.
3. Stay Silence — Stay with the silence that receives it, not with memory of the tone.
4. Let Surroundings — Let the next surroundings sound end the practice.
win: The tone disappeared completely and the next real sound, not the remembered one, ended the practice.
supports:
• Reset after slips; move the cue.
• Expect slips and restart quickly; reduce easy access to triggers.
• Notice the first automatic moment; make the new habit easier.
• Remove easy access; change the environment first.
• Keep replacement easy; interrupt the sequence.
formula_flow: Play Safe → Follow Decay → Stay Silence → Let Surroundings
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid intense volume or tones associated with distress.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

• Use a short focus block; take a real screen break.
• Use one window at a time; return after interruptions.
• Reduce background noise; keep one task visible.
• Reduce nearby noise; use one screen.

title: THE BREATH HINGE
goal: Feel the natural turning points of breathing without holding them open.
steps:
1. Follow Inhale — Follow a natural inhale to the instant it turns toward exhale.
2. Leave Hinge Free — Do not hold or stretch the hinge.
3. Change — Notice the same effortless change at the bottom of exhalation.
4. Allow Breaths — Visit each threshold lightly, then allow several breaths to pass unwatched.
win: Both breath hinges were noticed lightly and several later breaths were allowed to pass unwatched.
supports:
• Stop body scanning; use ordinary surroundings.
• Let breaths happen; loosen your shoulders.
• Avoid repeated pulse checking; stay somewhere physically safe.
• Keep your body supported; sit somewhere safe.
• Look at ordinary objects nearby; unclench your jaw and shoulders.
formula_flow: Follow Inhale → Leave Hinge Free → Change → Allow Breaths
safety:
PAUSE
Leave the hinge alone if waiting creates retention or air hunger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WHERE SOUND BECOMES HEARING
goal: Follow a sound toward the point where 'outside' becomes hearing.
steps:
1. Listen Sustained — Listen to a sustained, gentle sound.
2. Follow Apparent — Follow it from apparent distance toward the place where it becomes an auditory experience—ear, head, body, or nowhere locatable.
3. Rest Briefly — When the border between outside vibration and inside hearing blurs, rest there briefly.
win: The boundary between vibration out there and auditory experience in here became less definite for a moment.
supports:
• Wait before sending messages; do one steadying action.
• Let intensity fall; check the facts separately.
• Check basic needs; give the feeling time to move.
• Notice body tension; delay the message.
• Name the feeling plainly; use plain language.
formula_flow: Listen Sustained → Follow Apparent → Rest Briefly
safety:
PAUSE
Choose ordinary grounding if auditory focus feels intrusive or voice-like.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BORROW THE SKY’S WIDTH
goal: Widen your visual field enough to hold outer space and inner contraction together.
steps:
1. Open Sky — Gaze softly into open sky or another unobstructed safe field.
2. Release Pinpoint — Release pinpoint focus and include the edges of vision.
3. Compare Width — Without forcing calm, compare the width outside with the contraction inside.
4. Keep Wide View — Allow attention to occupy both.
win: Peripheral vision opened while the tightness inside remained allowed rather than forced away.
supports:
• Return after interruptions; silence nonessential notifications.
• Take a real screen break; keep one task visible.
• Put the phone out of reach; return to one target.
• Clear visual clutter; close extra tabs.
• Finish or park one open loop; use one screen.
formula_flow: Open Sky → Release Pinpoint → Compare Width → Keep Wide View
safety:
PAUSE
Never sky-gaze while driving or in unsafe light and weather.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CATCH WANTING BEFORE THE OBJECT
goal: Notice wanting before the object takes over the whole experience.
steps:
1. Wait Pull — Wait at the first pull: leaning, brightening, reaching, mental zoom.
2. Observe Wanting — For five seconds, observe wanting as raw movement without completing ‘I want…’.
3. Name Target — Only afterward name the desired thing and decide whether pursuit serves the wider situation.
win: The first pull was observed as movement before the desired thing was named or pursued.
supports:
• Reset without self-criticism; make the old habit harder.
• Replace one response; move the cue.
• Notice the first automatic moment; add small friction.
• Expect slips and restart quickly; interrupt the usual sequence.
• Change the environment; make the new habit easier.
formula_flow: Wait Pull → Observe Wanting → Name Target
safety:
PAUSE
Use added support for dangerous cravings or impaired control.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WATCH PLEASURE LEAVE CLEANLY
goal: Let a pleasant sensation fade completely without immediately reaching for another dose.
steps:

2. Track Rise — Track its rise, fullness, thinning, and the eventual return to neutral.

4. Let Pleasure Leave — Notice what remains when the pleasant signal is gone.
win: Pleasure rose, thinned, and returned toward neutral while you resisted topping it up.

• Make the old habit harder; notice the trigger.
• Reset without self-criticism; change the environment.
• Reset after slips; reduce easy access to triggers.
• Make the new habit easier; keep replacement easy.
• Notice the first automatic moment; change one cue.

title: NOT FOR, NOT AGAINST
goal: Release the inner pull or push around an experience before deciding what to do.
steps:
1. Check The Pull — Notice whether experience is being pulled closer or pushed away.
2. Relax — Relax the corresponding inner movement without demanding neutrality.
3. Let Content — Let the content remain unowned and unobstructed for a short interval.
4. Act According — Then act according to circumstance, not attraction or aversion.
win: The content remained briefly without being dragged closer or shoved away, then circumstance guided the action.
supports:
• Do one action for your life; limit social media exposure.
• Stop checking their numbers; notice what you cannot see.
• Compare with your past self; return to your own baseline.
• Choose your own measure; track progress by your values.
• Use your own priorities; name one thing already working.
formula_flow: Check The Pull → Relax → Let Content → Act According
safety:
PAUSE
Do not release practical action needed to protect health, rights, or safety.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WHO RECEIVED THAT THOUGHT?
goal: Follow the question of who received a thought without forcing an answer.
steps:
1. Ask Whom — When a thought appears, ask, ‘To whom did this occur?’ If ‘me’ appears, ask, ‘What is this me before the answer?’
2. Hold Question — Stay with the question’s open edge for several heartbeats.
win: The usual 'me' answer opened into a brief space where no further label had to be supplied.
supports:
• Notice the thought, then step back; use fewer words.
• Stop debating; do not debate every detail.
• Use present facts; keep one task.
• Reduce commentary; let the thought stay unfinished.
• Notice the thought; leave it unfinished.
formula_flow: Ask Whom → Hold Question
safety:
PAUSE
Return to concrete sense of where you are if inquiry feels ungrounding.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: REMOVE THE NAME BADGES
goal: Set your active roles down briefly, then pick up only the one the next situation needs.
steps:
1. Spot Loudest Role — Notice which role is speaking loudest right now.
2. Set Badges Down — Imagine placing each active badge on a table—parent, worker, partner, achiever, patient, helper, or another role that fits.
3. Pause Without Label — Sit for a short pause without using any badge to answer “Who am I now?”
4. Reclaim One Role — Reclaim only the role the next situation actually needs.
win: Several identity badges became optional for a moment instead of all speaking at once.
supports:
• Change one cue; reduce easy access to triggers.
• Use the same replacement repeatedly; remove easy access.
• Reset without self-criticism; add small friction.
• Expect slips and restart quickly; replace one response.
• Delay the routine; notice the trigger.
formula_flow: Spot Loudest Role → Set Badges Down → Pause Without Label → Reclaim One Role
safety:
PAUSE
Keep grounding and avoid role stripping if identity feels fragile.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PUT THE FEELINGS BACK IN ORDER
goal: Put blended feelings back into the order they actually arrived.
steps:
1. Name Mix — Name up to three present feelings. Do not explain them yet.
2. Find First — Which arrived first? Put it at the left of a short line.
3. Link Cue — Add the concrete cue that each feeling answered—words heard, an image, a body change, or a later thought.
4. Read Order — Read the sequence once: ‘First ___ answered ___; then ___ answered ___.’ Stop after the order is clear.
win: Each emotion was linked to its own cue, making the sequence clearer without needing a bigger story.
supports:
• Avoid decisions at peak emotion; use plain language.
• Wait before sending messages; check basic needs.
• Name the feeling plainly; lower stimulation for a minute.
• Delay the message; use simple words for the problem.
• Notice what changed physically; eat, drink, or rest if needed.
formula_flow: Name Mix → Find First → Link Cue → Read Order
safety:
PAUSE
Stop if sequencing pulls you into flashback, self-blame, numbness, or forced certainty about the past.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

4. Read Order — Read the sequence once: ‘First ___ answered ___; then ___ answered ___.’ Stop after the order is clear.

WIN
Each emotion was linked to its own cue, making the sequence clearer without needing a bigger story.

• Avoid decisions at peak emotion; use plain language.
• Wait before sending messages; check basic needs.
• Name the feeling plainly; lower stimulation for a minute.
• Delay the message; use simple words for the problem.
• Notice what changed physically; eat, drink, or rest if needed.

MIND BEND
Feelings that arrive seconds apart can fuse into one verdict; restoring order shows that they may be answering different events.

FORMULA FLOW
Name Mix → Find First → Link Cue → Read Order

SAFETY
PAUSE
Stop if sequencing pulls you into flashback, self-blame, numbness, or forced certainty about the past.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE SIX-LINK FIRE CHAIN
goal: Trace anger backward to the earliest link where fuel can still be removed.
steps:
1. Trace Sequence — Trace the sequence backward: confusion or loss of judgement; anger; frustrated desire; attachment; repeated attention; original cue.

win: The chain led past the heat to one reachable cue, demand, attachment, or attention loop you could change.
supports:
• Clarify the deadline; end with action.
• Ask what they understood; name the desired change.
• Avoid guessing their intent; keep one issue per conversation.
• Separate facts from tone; lead with the point.
• Check the agreed deadline; use one concrete example.

title: DO NOT REPLACE THE LAST THOUGHT
goal: Let one thought end without immediately filling the empty beat with another.
steps:
1. Wait Thought — Wait for a thought to end naturally.
2. Empty — At the first empty beat, resist generating commentary about emptiness.
3. Rest Duration — Rest for the duration available—even a fraction.
4. Let Thought — Let the next thought arise without invitation.
5. Count Gap — Count the gap only after it is over.
win: A real gap appeared before the next thought arrived on its own, even if it lasted only a fraction.
supports:
• Choose tiny action; remove one barrier.
• Make it visible; open only what you need.
• Stop planning after one action; use two minutes.
• Reward starting, not finishing; shrink the first action.
• Skip extra setup; enter through easy work.
formula_flow: Wait Thought → Empty → Rest Duration → Let Thought → Count Gap
safety:
PAUSE
Use external engagement if silence feels frightening or destabilising.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: PAY FOR THE NEXT LAP
goal: Make another thinking lap pay for the time it takes from real life.
steps:
1. Name Lap — Name the exact question you want one more thinking lap to answer. One sentence only.
2. Price Trade — Choose what those three minutes will replace: rest, a message, food, movement, work, or a decision. Say the trade plainly.
3. Buy Three — If the trade is worth it, set three minutes and think only about the named question. If not, close the lap now.
4. Close Toll — When the clock ends, stop without buying another lap. Do the displaced activity or deliberately let it go.
win: The exact question and its trade-off were named before three minutes of thinking were either bought or declined.
supports:
• Return to one physical task; leave unsolved questions.
• End the replay; set a clear stopping point.
• Change rooms if possible; stop solving the unsolvable.
• Name one useful action; ask if any new information exists.
• Stop repeated review; return to current task.
formula_flow: Name Lap → Price Trade → Buy Three → Close Toll
safety:
PAUSE
Never buy another analysis lap with sleep, medication, food, immediate safety, or time-critical responsibilities.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

The exact question and its trade-off were named before three minutes of thinking were either bought or declined.

• Return to one physical task; leave unsolved questions.

• Stop repeated review; return to current task.

title: PUT THE MEMORY BACK IN PAST TENSE
goal: Put one memory segment into past tense while inserting present facts between loaded lines.
steps:
1. Use Happened — Retell one short segment using was, happened, had, and then.
2. Ground Between — After every emotionally loaded sentence, insert three present facts: your present location, the current year, and what choice exists now.
3. Finish Moment — Finish with: ‘That ended; this moment is different.’
win: The retelling repeatedly returned to current place, year, and available choice before ending in today's reality.
supports:
• Slow physical pace; do one steadying action.
• Lower stimulation for a minute; name the feeling plainly.
• Eat, drink, or rest if needed; separate feeling from fact.
• Rest before deciding; lower nearby noise.
• Name the emotion; check the facts separately.
formula_flow: Use Happened → Ground Between → Finish Moment
safety:
PAUSE
Do not retell alone if the memory overwhelms sense of where you are.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THREE SELVES, THREE JOBS
goal: Put past actions, present repairs, and future prevention back into their correct time zones.
steps:
1. Make Time Zones — Picture three time zones: PAST, PRESENT, FUTURE.
2. Complete Actions — Place completed actions in PAST, available repair in PRESENT, and prevention plans in FUTURE.
3. Reassign — Move any item that belongs to the wrong time zone.
4. Do Present Job — Do only one PRESENT task now.
win: Misplaced tasks moved to the right period, leaving one genuinely present action to do now.
supports:
• Lower standards briefly; choose a rough beginning.
• Do the easiest useful part; start with one minute.
• Prepare first; start physically.
• Set a two-minute timer; prepare the task in advance.
• Lower the first demand; make it visible.

safety:
PAUSE
Do not use time ownership to evade current accountability for earlier harm.

title: PUT THE YEARS BACK BETWEEN THEM
goal: Restore the real time distance between events that currently feel piled together.
steps:
1. Date Events — Picture the dates of the events that currently feel piled together.
2. Scale Distance — Give equal physical space to equal spans of time; do not place every event in one crowded cluster.
3. Present — Notice TODAY at the correct distance and name one fact that belongs only to now.
4. Recheck Urgency — Look again at the oldest event and rate how immediate it feels after the spacing is restored.
win: Older events moved back along the timeline, and one fact belonging only to today regained its proper place.
supports:
• Ignore imagined regret; reduce the options.
• Keep new facts separate; limit the options.
• Choose the option you can support; commit once chosen.
• Choose reversible first; set a deadline.
• Ask what failure would cost; stop extra research.

safety:
PAUSE
Stop and reorient to the room if the timeline makes the past feel more present.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

4. Recheck Urgency — Look again at the oldest event and rate how immediate it feels after the spacing is restored.

WIN
Older events moved back along the timeline, and one fact belonging only to today regained its proper place.

• Ignore imagined regret; reduce the options.
• Keep new facts separate; limit the options.
• Choose the option you can support; commit once chosen.
• Choose reversible first; set a deadline.
• Ask what failure would cost; stop extra research.

MIND BEND
The mind can compress years into one emotional cluster. Spacing time visually reduces the false message that everything is happening now.

Date Events → Scale Distance → Present → Recheck Urgency

SAFETY
PAUSE
Stop and reorient to the room if the timeline makes the past feel more present.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THIRD-PERSON OWNERSHIP TEST
goal: Step back from the mind's content without stepping away from the action you own.
steps:
1. Describe Event — Frame the moment once as ‘this mind is predicting…’ or ‘the system is producing…’.
2. Change — Notice what changes in intensity, responsibility, and choice.
3. Return Person — Then return to first person for the action you really own: ‘I will…’.
4. Loosen the Grammar — Distance the content, not agency.
win: The prediction was described at a distance, then first-person agency returned exactly where behaviour began.
supports:
• Lower standards briefly; shrink the first action.
• Reward starting, not finishing; use one window.
• Remove one obvious distraction; prepare first.
• Cut the task; enter through easy work.
• Restart quickly; make it visible.

safety:
PAUSE
Stop if altered pronouns increase estrangement from self.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ZOOM LENS TRAINING
goal: Practise moving attention between tiny detail and the whole scene.
steps:
1. Imagine Shape — Picture one simple shape.
2. Zoom Detail — Spend ten slow counts on one tiny feature.
3. Widen View — Spend ten counts on the whole shape and the space around it.
4. Reverse — Move back to detail, then choose the view that best fits your task.
win: You could zoom in, zoom out, and deliberately choose the view that fit the task.
supports:
• Delay the verdict; question absolute words.
• Check what you actually know; use a real example.
• Check the base rate; test the assumption.
• Notice absolute words like always; ask what else could fit.
• Check the whole situation; ask what would change your mind.
formula_flow: Imagine Shape → Zoom Detail → Widen View → Reverse
safety:
PAUSE
Use broad awareness in environments that require hazard monitoring.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE PRICE OF KEEPING THIS SELF
goal: Measure what a self-concept permits, blocks, and demands before deciding whether it still serves you.
steps:
1. Sort Identity Costs — Imagine three buckets: IT LETS ME; IT STOPS ME; IT DEMANDS FROM ME.
2. Fill The Buckets — Mentally sort the self-concept into those three buckets.
3. Find The Price — Focus on the highest hidden cost and ask whether the identity still earns its keep.
win: The hidden cost became visible enough to question whether keeping the identity was worth its price.
supports:
• Cut the task; make the first move tiny.
• Set a two-minute timer; shrink the first action.
• Reward starting, not finishing; lower the first demand.
• Open the task; do the easiest useful part.
• Remove one barrier; skip extra setup.
formula_flow: Sort Identity Costs → Fill The Buckets → Find The Price
safety:
PAUSE
Preserve identities that provide community, protection, or meaning unless change is genuinely chosen.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CALL THE INNER COUNCIL
goal: Let different inner needs speak once, then give coordination to the part protecting the whole system.

title: ADD THE WITNESS WHO SHOULD HAVE BEEN THERE
goal: Add the protective witness who should have named what was wrong and what you deserved.
steps:
1. Introduce — Introduce a compassionate observer appropriate to the event—a trusted adult, advocate, elder, clinician, or current-you.
2. Name Wrong — Have them name what was wrong, what protection was deserved, and what is true about the person who endured it.
3. Keep It Believable — Keep their words believable.
win: A believable observer supplied protection, truth, and context that the original scene had lacked.
supports:
• Keep one real task in view; reduce commentary.
• Let the thought stay unfinished; avoid building a larger story.
• Drop the need to solve it; let it pass.
• Use fewer words about it; keep one task.
• Notice the thought, then step back; stop debating.
formula_flow: Introduce → Name Wrong → Keep It Believable
safety:
PAUSE
Use guided trauma work if imagined witnessing intensifies grief or flashback.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RELATIONSHIP DATA, NOT ONE BIG FEELING
goal: Review a relationship as separate events, frequency, context, repair, and outcomes.
steps:
1. Hold Event — Keep the event, context, frequency, repair attempt, and outcome as separate mental snapshots. Feel the surface supporting you.
2. Look Repetition — Look for repetition and exceptions.
3. Issue Narrow — Make a narrow conclusion about the observed period instead of using ‘always’ or ‘never’.
win: Patterns and exceptions both stayed visible, producing a narrow conclusion instead of 'always' or 'never'.
supports:
• Ask what else could fit; check another angle.
• Delay major conclusions when upset; question absolute words.
• Use recent, concrete evidence; delay the verdict.
• Separate guess from evidence; check the base rate.
• Check the whole situation; test the assumption.
formula_flow: Hold Event → Look Repetition → Issue Narrow
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use data collection to remain in an unsafe relationship.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: APOLOGY NEEDS THREE EVIDENCE POINTS
goal: Judge an apology by acknowledgement, changed action, and prevention evidence over time.
steps:
1. Return Define — Define what adequate repair requires: clear acknowledgement, changed action, and prevention of return.
2. Specify — Specify what evidence would show each over time.
3. Evaluate — Check the apology against those criteria rather than immediate emotion.
win: Repair was measured against three observable criteria rather than the emotion of the moment.
supports:
• Wait before sending messages; give the feeling time to move.
• Let intensity fall; rest before deciding.
• Use simple words for the problem; delay the message.
• Separate feeling from fact; notice body tension.
• Do one steadying action; check the facts separately.
formula_flow: Return Define → Specify → Evaluate
safety:
PAUSE
No repair test obliges renewed contact after serious harm.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: SET THE CONTACT DOSE
goal: Choose the smallest contact dose that preserves both connection and regulation.
steps:
1. Choose Frequency — Before contact, choose frequency, duration, permitted topics, location, and exit phrase.
2. Start Lowest — Start with the lowest dose that preserves both connection and regulation.
3. Use Body — Review afterward using body and behaviour, not guilt.
win: Frequency, duration, topic, location, and exit were set before contact and reviewed using body plus behaviour afterward.
supports:
• Add the missing context; ask what else could fit.
• Ask what would change your mind; test the assumption.
• Use current facts; check another angle.
• Look for one missing fact; check what you actually know.
• Check the whole situation; separate guess from evidence.
formula_flow: Choose Frequency → Start Lowest → Use Body
safety:
PAUSE
Reduce or end contact when boundaries are ignored or safety is compromised.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ONE FOCUS MARK
goal: Mute the strongest distraction and give one task a short, protected timer.
steps:

win: The interval ended with evidence of what moved rather than a vague sense of having tried to focus.
supports:
• Reduce nearby noise; clear visual clutter.
• Silence nonessential notifications; return to one target.
• Protect one focus block; mute alerts.
• Return after interruptions; choose one target.
• Put the phone out of reach; take a short break.

goal: Separate the need from the interpretation before deciding when this choice should be reviewed.

title: THE SIGNAL FIRST
goal: Stop feeding the body-check loop and move toward another person.
steps:
1. Look Around — Name two sides of the room.
2. Name Signal — Call the body signal a wave.
3. Cross Room — Walk slowly toward the farther side.
4. Text Someone — Contact one trusted person now.
win: The sensation was labelled as a wave, your body moved through the room, and trusted contact replaced repeated checking.
supports:
• Let breaths happen; wait out the surge.
• Avoid symptom searching; reduce caffeine.
• Stay somewhere physically safe; look at ordinary objects nearby.
• Keep your body supported; reduce extra stimulation.
• Give the surge time to pass; keep movements gentle.
formula_flow: Look Around → Name Signal → Cross Room → Text Someone
safety:
PAUSE
Keep your eyes open and orient to the room. Stop if symptoms intensify, you feel faint, or a medical problem may be possible. Call Triple Zero (000) for an emergency; otherwise use qualified medical advice. Do not induce or test symptoms.
This is brief self-help, not diagnosis or treatment.

title: GROUND BEFORE THE MESSAGE
goal: Lower the body's speed enough to choose a steady message instead of a pressured one.
steps:
1. Hold Choice — Let the first pressure pass without acting.
2. Cool Pace — Slow your body one notch.
3. Unmix Story — Separate what happened from what you fear it means.
4. Set Limit — Say how much capacity is genuinely available right now.
5. Make Sentence — Choose one steady sentence you can send without hurrying.
win: The facts, feared meaning, and available capacity separated before one sendable sentence was chosen.
supports:
• Return when your body settles; use one clear request.
• Avoid empty threats; return when calmer.
• Use one request; avoid adding old grievances.
• Name the exact issue; do not send the message yet.
• Stick to current facts; name the issue.
formula_flow: Hold Choice → Cool Pace → Unmix Story → Set Limit → Make Sentence
safety:
PAUSE
Do not send, drive, confront, threaten, or act while control feels reduced. Move away from weapons and hazards; use human or emergency support if anyone may be unsafe.
This is brief self-help, not treatment or emergency care.

title: TREAT THIS AS MEDICAL NOW
play_time: ACT NOW — MOVE TO LIVE SUPPORT
goal: Treat severe or worsening withdrawal symptoms as a medical issue and get urgent care.
steps:
1. Stop Every Exercise — End breathing, movement, or mental exercises immediately.
2. Avoid Driving — Sit somewhere safe and do not drive yourself for care.
3. Call Medical Help — Call 000 for severe symptoms or rapidly worsening withdrawal.
4. Share Key Facts — Tell responders about substances, medicines, symptoms, and timing.
5. Stay Observable — Remain with another person where changes can be noticed.
win: Self-help stopped, another person stayed nearby, and emergency responders received the substance, medicine, symptom, and timing information they needed.
supports:
• Get urgent medical assessment now.
• Do not drive if you feel unsafe.
• Tell someone what is happening.
• Stay with another person if possible.
• Follow professional medical advice.
formula_flow: Stop Every Exercise → Avoid Driving → Call Medical Help → Share Key Facts → Stay Observable
safety:
PAUSE
IMMEDIATE DANGER OR POSSIBLE MEDICAL EMERGENCY: call Triple Zero (000) now.
24/7 CRISIS SUPPORT: call Lifeline 13 11 14 or text 0477 13 11 14.
Stay with a safe person and follow qualified support. Do not return to ordinary rituals.

title: WHO YOU CHOOSE NEXT
goal: Keep a disturbing thought separate from identity and let the next chosen action represent you instead.
steps:
1. Catch Thought — Catch the thought without explaining it.
2. Unhook Identity — Say, “My mind produced this; it is not my biography.”
3. Name Value — Name one value you want to stand for in the next minute—kind, honest, patient, careful, brave, or another word that fits.
4. Act Value — Do one ten-second action that matches that principle.
5. Leave Unanswered — Leave the thought unanswered and continue with the action.
win: A value was named and a ten-second action expressed it while the thought remained unanswered.
supports:
• Delay reassurance; avoid confessing for relief.
• Return to the task; notice it as mental content.
• Reduce deliberate monitoring; let thoughts pass.
• Skip confession for relief; avoid testing what it means.
• Avoid meaning tests; let uncertainty remain.
formula_flow: Catch Thought → Unhook Identity → Name Value → Act Value → Leave Unanswered
safety:
